newsitem.title: UK: ICCO panel fixes cocoa stock/grind ratio at 34 pct.
newsitem.headline: ICCO panel fixes cocoa stock/grind ratio at 34 pct.

text.p: An International Cocoa Organization committee on Thursday agreed to fix the world cocoa stock-to-grind ratio, the basis of ICCO production controls, at 34 percent by the end of the 1998/99 crop year, delegates at a meeting said.
They said the accord was subject to endorsement at an ICCO council session on Friday.
"We feel that the ratio is least destructive to the market," a producer spokesman said.
The ratio -- a barometer of prices -- is the basis of the 36-member ICCO's supply control measures.

No new output goals were immediately set for 1996/97 crop year but the ICCO's so-called production management plan foresees a 375,000-tonne cut in world output over five years from 1994 to balance supply and demand. The ratio was among vexed issues at the weeklong ICCO meeting in London.
Producers had insisted on a ratio of 32 percent but consumers disagreed.

Historically, cocoa prices have taken an upturn each time the ratio falls below a 30 percent threshold. The difference between 34 and 32 percent would mean equivalent to an extra 20,000 tonnes of cocoa in the first year.
